writeup: TIC 349116460 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.2968 days. The TESS photometry shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.69 percent dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 109.5. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 26.1, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel object. The automated pipeline's machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.51, and the data passed all quality checks without flags. Further observations would help establish whether this candidate is a genuine eclipsing binary system.
